compiled_state.description:
## Problem

rebar's LLM gates (`review-plan`, `review-code`, `verify-completion`) pin their config read-root to an attested snapshot so a parallel branch switch cannot change a verdict mid-review. That snapshot is materialised with `git checkout-index --all`, which writes only tracked files.

The project config this repository supplies to the rebar CLI is the root `rebar.toml`, which is untracked by its own mandate. Its header states it must never land on a tracked branch or in `.gitignore`, and `.git/info/exclude` line 10 carries it. It is therefore absent from every gate snapshot.

rebar finds no `[llm]` table, falls back to its built-in model-class defaults, and those default to direct Anthropic. With no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` present every gate call fails and the gate returns INDETERMINATE. Bedrock is never attempted.

The failure is silent. The warning names only the fallback model, so the operator sees an authentication error for a provider the project never configured.

## Evidence

Materialising a snapshot exactly as rebar does and running its own reader against it.

```
git checkout-index --all --prefix=$T/
test -f $T/rebar.toml                 -> absent
_read_llm_file_table($T)              -> {}
```

Against the working checkout the same reader returns the full Bedrock table, which is why `rebar create`, `rebar edit`, and every `verify.*` setting resolve correctly. Only the gates are affected.

`config/local/rebar-review.toml` is tracked, is present in the snapshot, and its reader returns the platform tier table. A plan-review gate pointed at it ran on `bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0`, so the approach is already demonstrated.

## Approach

The platform already solved this for its review worker. `compose.yaml` sets `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` to `/app/config/local/rebar-review.toml`, a deliberate decision recorded as KTD2 in the native Bedrock review path plan. Host-side gate runs are the only path that never got the same treatment.

Give the host the same wiring through `invoke`, following the `operator_done` precedent of a host task that supplies the environment the host needs through `c.run(env=...)`.

The config path is derived from `tasks.py`'s own location rather than the process working directory, because `invoke` locates `tasks.py` by walking up from the caller's directory and then runs the command in that caller's directory. An `abspath` of a relative path would resolve against the wrong root whenever the operator invokes from a subdirectory. rebar treats a `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` that does not exist as a hard error rather than a silent fallback, so a wrong path surfaces immediately instead of degrading the way the current discovery gap does. No extra handling is added on top of that, because rebar's own exit status already propagates through `c.run`.

Reuse `config/local/rebar-review.toml` rather than adding a second config. It is pinned to the same tier table as `config/local/litellm-config.yaml`, so a fork would drift from the platform's configured models. It also keeps its fallback legs on Bedrock (`us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0`), where the root `rebar.toml` falls back to an unauthenticated `anthropic:` leg, which is the exact mechanism that made this failure silent.

Add the missing `trivial` class to `config/local/rebar-review.toml`. rebar's plan-review ladder has a cheapest rung whose built-in default is a bare `claude-haiku-4-5` that infers direct Anthropic. Today's usage log shows every call landing on `frontier` or `standard`, so the rung is unexercised, but it is the same latent trap and the review worker shares it. Pin it to `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`, matching the `classification-summary` tier in `config/local/litellm-config.yaml`.

`tests/unit/test_tasks.py` holds an `EXPECTED_TASKS` set and asserts exact equality against `ns.task_names` at line 60, so both new task names must be added to that set in the same change or the existing test fails.

Strip the now-duplicated `[llm]` block from the untracked root `rebar.toml` so the tier table has one source of truth. That file is untracked, so it does not appear in the diff.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `config/local/rebar-review.toml` defines a `trivial` model class on the Bedrock provider with model `us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0`. Proved by a test asserting all three class names parse with provider `bedrock`.
- [ ] No model class in `config/local/rebar-review.toml` resolves to a non-Bedrock provider on any primary or fallback leg, so no gate leg can reach an unauthenticated direct-Anthropic endpoint. Proved by the same test walking every primary and fallback.
- [ ] The `trivial` primary matches the `classification-summary` model id in `config/local/litellm-config.yaml`, so the rebar tier table and the gateway tier table do not drift. Proved by a test reading both files and comparing.
- [ ] `invoke` exposes `rebar-review-plan`, which runs rebar's plan-review gate with `REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE` set and accepts an optional gate ref for reviewing against a stack base. Checked by `inv --list` listing the task.
- [ ] `invoke` exposes `rebar-review-code`, taking a base and a head. Checked by `inv --list` listing the task.
- [ ] The config path handed to rebar is absolute and derived from the location of `tasks.py`, so invoking from a subdirectory still resolves it. Proved by a test that changes the working directory to a subdirectory and asserts the produced path is unchanged and absolute.
- [ ] `EXPECTED_TASKS` in `tests/unit/test_tasks.py` gains both task names, so the existing exact-set assertion at line 60 passes and proves both tasks are registered on the collection. Proved by `pytest tests/unit/test_tasks.py`.
- [ ] A gate run against this repository resolves a Bedrock model rather than a direct-Anthropic one. Proved by `inv rebar-review-plan --ticket 001a-779a-81e8-456b` reporting a `model` beginning `bedrock:`.
- [ ] The README documents the host gate recipe and states why the config file must be named explicitly. Checked by reading the section.
- [ ] The change introduces no lint regression. Proved by `ruff check .`.

## Testing

- A new unit test over `config/local/rebar-review.toml` covering the three classes, the Bedrock-only invariant across primaries and fallbacks, and the id match against `config/local/litellm-config.yaml`.
- A new unit test asserting the config path helper is absolute and independent of the working directory.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_tasks.py` proves both tasks are registered, through the existing exact-set assertion.
- `ruff check .` covers lint.
- The full suite is the regression net, because `tasks.py` is imported by the existing task tests.

## Out of scope

Bumping the tier table from the 4-5 generation to 4-8 and 4-6. The rebar tier table is pinned to `config/local/litellm-config.yaml`, so moving it is a platform-wide model decision that must change both files together and revalidate the review worker.

Making rebar discover an untracked project config inside a gate. That is rebar's behaviour and the snapshot is deliberate, so the fix belongs upstream rather than here.

Add _host_rebar_env plus rebar-review-plan and rebar-review-code tasks and register them on the collection
Document the host gate recipe and why REBAR_LLM_CONFIG_FILE must be named explicitly
New tests for the three classes, the Bedrock-only invariant, and the id match against litellm-config.yaml
Assert both gate tasks resolve through the invoke collection
